items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: Grandma Bessie was a Christian Scientist and it was a very wacky religion and Grandpa Pete believed in baked beans, stars, and rattlesnakes.

ctx.x: Yeah. And his dad was a cowboy and so he had ethics and morality that were very much right down the line of like he would never have done anything that wasn’t sort of Biblically correct in a certain way. But it wasn’t through a religious following, it was through life experience. You know you don’t treat someone like that because it will come back to get you. Or you don’t — he had, wouldn’t you say that you know he just had this kind of —

Yeah and Judeo-Christian ethical morality thing was strong in his blood. You know? And Grandma Bessie was a Christian Scientist and it was a very wacky religion and Grandpa Pete believed in baked beans, stars, and rattlesnakes. But you combine those two — and you know World War II was a deep experience for my dad and that’s when he vowed to himself “I want to get the tools so I can write a huge orchestral choral piece with Biblical text that somehow does this thing about somehow changing hearts and minds so we…

like “Saving Private Ryan” and the horror show of that that was portrayed so beautifully or horribly in that movie. You know he still saw plenty of horrible things and met lots of people and met lots of just regular Germans who thought what happened to our country? You know how the hell did this guy Adolf Hitler completely take us and throw us into this horrible thing and we ended up killing millions of people. And they all believe that Christ is their savior. Like how is that happening and they’re bombing. You…
